articles.title: IndexedDB in React: Offline-First Apps with WatermelonDB
articles.excerpt: Originally published at muhammadmoiz.dev. IndexedDB is the browser's built-in database. It is the right place to keep the data a React app needs to keep working when the network drops. You can use it…
articles.body: Originally published at muhammadmoiz.dev . IndexedDB is the browser's built-in database. It is the right place to keep the data a React app needs to keep working when the network drops. You can use it directly through a small wrapper like idb for simple caching. If you need relations, reactive queries and two-way sync with a server, put WatermelonDB on top of it. This tutorial walks through both approaches, with code you can adapt. I used WatermelonDB on browser storage to build the offline-first data layer of Oscar, a restaurant and retail POS. A POS can't stop taking orders just because the Wi-Fi went down. The patterns below are the ones I'd reach for again. If you want the product-level story first, read lessons from building an offline-first POS in React .

articles.title: The Graph Behind a Four-Letter Word Ladder
articles.excerpt: A four-letter word ladder looks like a word game. Underneath, it is a shortest-path problem on an unweighted graph, and thinking about it that way explains most of the difficulty. The graph has every…
articles.body: A four-letter word ladder looks like a word game. Underneath, it is a shortest-path problem on an unweighted graph, and thinking about it that way explains most of the difficulty. The graph has every valid four-letter word as a node. Two nodes share an edge if they differ in exactly one letter. The daily puzzle picks a start word, fixes the target (POOP), and asks for a route. Par is the length of the shortest path the game has checked. Once you model it that way, the strange parts of the game become obvious. Some starting words have very few neighbours, so the first move is constrained. Vowel changes jump between clusters, so they behave like hub edges. And a legal word can be a dead end, because legal nodes can have degree one.

articles.title: How to Test a Resistor, Diode, LED and Capacitor with a Multimeter (Before You Blame Your Code)
articles.excerpt: If you write code for Arduino or ESP32, you have probably spent an evening debugging a sketch that was fine all along. The real bug was a dead LED, a reversed diode or a dried-out capacitor. A cheap d…
articles.body: If you write code for Arduino or ESP32, you have probably spent an evening debugging a sketch that was fine all along. The real bug was a dead LED, a reversed diode or a dried-out capacitor. A cheap digital multimeter catches all of these in about two minutes. Here are the four checks I teach every beginner: resistor, diode, LED and capacitor . For each one: which mode, where the probes go, and what a good and a bad reading look like. Before you start Test parts out of the circuit, with no power . A part still soldered to a board reads wrong because other parts sit in parallel with it. Discharge capacitors first. Big ones from power supplies, TVs or inverters can hold a dangerous charge. Practise on small capacitors rated 50 V or less. Black probe in COM , red probe in VΩ .

articles.title: Loopback Is Not a Trust Boundary for Todoist's HTTP MCP Server
articles.excerpt: Loopback Is Not a Trust Boundary for Todoist's HTTP MCP Server Local AI tool servers are often treated as safe because they bind to 127.0.0.1. CVE-2026-76807 shows why network location and caller iden…
articles.body: Loopback Is Not a Trust Boundary for Todoist's HTTP MCP Server Local AI tool servers are often treated as safe because they bind to 127.0.0.1 . CVE-2026-76807 shows why network location and caller identity are different controls. What went wrong Todoist MCP versions through 10.3.2 exposed an optional todoist-mcp-http server. The server accepted browser-origin MCP requests without validating Host or Origin and without requiring a caller secret. DNS rebinding allowed a malicious public website to route its own hostname to the victim's loopback listener. The server then executed tools with its configured TODOIST_API_KEY .

articles.title: The Invisible Type: Three Escapes of size_t from Linux CI
articles.excerpt: Unlike int or float, in C++ the size_t type is not a built-in language keyword. It is a regular typedef that lives in system header files (for example, ). However, in real projects, developers often u…
articles.body: Unlike int or float , in C++ the size_t type is not a built-in language keyword. It is a regular typedef that lives in system header files (for example, <cstddef> ). However, in real projects, developers often use size_t "naked," without an explicit #include , relying on transitive inclusion from other files. The old Doxygen parser we were stuck on before didn't care about this—it worked like a regular expression and simply read text. But when we switched to a true AST parser (via libclang ), the compiler demanded strictness. And so began one of the most ridiculous quests in the history of our CI. Escape One: Silent Annihilation We wrote tests for the new parser, ran them locally on Windows—everything was green.

articles.title: 7,472 write bursts and 48,216 rows: what a prediction log can and cannot prove
articles.excerpt: Every prediction platform eventually has to answer one question from a customer, a regulator, or its own postmortem: was this row produced by an analysis of this match, or was it replayed? The model c…
articles.body: Every prediction platform eventually has to answer one question from a customer, a regulator, or its own postmortem: was this row produced by an analysis of this match, or was it replayed? The model card describes intent, not execution. The only artifact describing execution is the row itself — its write time, its measured duration, its payload. So I treated our own production log as a forensic object. The table is ai_predictions : 48,216 rows, 47,167 graded, 3,853 models, 17,235 matches, 116 distinct days from 2026-06-21 to 2026-11-20. Orientation: 26,806 hits over 47,167 graded rows, 56.83%. Cluster the writes into bursts A prediction is not an event, it is a member of a batch. To see batches you do not need a job table — you need the gap between consecutive writes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth. Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway. Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010 . Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa.

articles.excerpt: A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a tower's-eye view of the first-ever catch of a Starship upper stage, a milestone SpaceX achieved last weekend.
articles.body: A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage. The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms. You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) "The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship.

articles.title: No more asteroid landing: Engine trouble forces Japan's Hayabusa2 probe to change plans
articles.excerpt: Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 asteroid mission, due to problems with the spacecraft's ion thrusters.
articles.body: Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 mission, due to the spacecraft suffering trouble with its ion thrusters. The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu . Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end.

articles.title: China rolls out rocket for launch of 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station (video)
articles.excerpt: China has rolled to the launch pad the rocket and spacecraft for its Shenzhou-24 mission, which will fly the first international astronaut to the nation's Tiangong space station.
articles.body: China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut. A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week. The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026.
